claims.title: Exact rational belief-state Bellman recursion for stochastic law observations
claims.scope: finite rational hidden law states, rational Markov transitions, rational stochastic observation kernels, deterministic zero-error prefix-code actions, finite horizon, and rational switching penalties
assumptions: the current observation is emitted before the current code choice
code actions do not affect hidden transitions or observation probabilities
the initial prior and all model probabilities are known exactly
all reachable belief nodes and positive-probability branches complete below configured caps
nonclaims: the theorem supplies no statistical coverage for the model probabilities
the model minimizes expected cost rather than a worst-case hidden path
the result is not evidence for simulation or a parent-resource bound

claims.title: Exact posterior belief and previous code are sufficient controller state in the declared hidden Markov coding model
claims.scope: public histories in the same finite hidden Markov source model that induce equal posterior beliefs and equal previous code actions
assumptions: hidden transitions and observations are conditionally Markov under the supplied matrices
future transition and observation laws are code-independent
stage cost depends on the hidden state only through the declared source law and selected code
nonclaims: belief sufficiency fails if omitted history variables affect transitions, observations, or costs
a Bayesian posterior is not interchangeable with a frequentist confidence region or robust information set

claims.title: Blackwell garbling cannot improve minimum expected coding cost
claims.scope: two finite rational observation experiments where the coarse kernel equals the fine kernel followed by a row-stochastic garbling channel
assumptions: the hidden law model, initial prior, action set, horizon, and switching cost are held fixed
source-independent private randomization may be used to simulate the garbled signal
finite expected-cost belief control admits a deterministic optimal policy
nonclaims: the theorem does not price acquiring, storing, or communicating the finer signal
a finer signal need not provide a strict improvement
the result assumes the declared probabilistic model is correct

claims.title: Exact rational Bayes observation and prediction updates preserve the finite probability simplex
claims.scope: positive-probability observations in a finite rational hidden Markov model
assumptions: the supplied prior, transition rows, and observation rows are probability vectors
zero-probability observations are excluded from the reachable branch tree
nonclaims: exact arithmetic conditional on supplied probabilities is not evidence that those probabilities are empirically exact
the update does not address unknown parameters or model misspecification

claims.title: Static point-mass K3 has strict no, partial, and full expected-observation values
claims.scope: uniform prior over three static point-mass hidden law states, complete confusion K3, two periods, no switching penalty, and observation kernels none, partition {1}{23}, and full
assumptions: complete binary prefix codes have length vectors that are permutations of (1,2,2)
the hidden law state remains fixed and observations arrive before code choices
nonclaims: the values 10/3, 8/3, and 2 are specific to the declared finite model
the example does not estimate an observation value from data

claims.title: Reveal-or-unknown K3 garbling has exact one-period value four thirds
claims.scope: uniform static point-mass K3 where the exact state label is revealed with probability one half and an uninformative symbol is emitted otherwise
assumptions: the reveal-or-unknown channel is independent conditional on the hidden state
the horizon is one period and switching cost is zero
nonclaims: the exact gains of one third are specific to this channel and prior
the noisy signal is a model input rather than a measured sensor specification

claims.title: Bounded exact Bayesian belief-tree and garbling audit
claims.scope: the rational Bayes-update, deterministic partition, stochastic garbling, K3 expected-cost, switching, and cap instances exercised by repository tests
assumptions: the deterministic code universe, reachable beliefs, and observation branches complete below configured caps
all supplied model probabilities and dynamic-program values use exact rational arithmetic
nonclaims: bounded finite agreement is not a continuous-state or scalability theorem
CI success does not provide empirical support for simulation
